experiments.name: Multi-agent throughput
experiments.hypothesis: running six agents in parallel produces more than running one
experiments.method: six lanes against a solo baseline, preregistered, sum of per-lane durations
experiments.result: 1.08x the output for 3.2x the compute, 955 agent-seconds against 297
experiments.note: write-up lives in fleet-ops, which is private. The tool and its findings are public at github.com/Morkeeth/fleet; this specific measurement is not yet.

experiments.name: Harness premium, Terminal-Bench 2.1
experiments.hypothesis: a model's native scaffold beats a model-agnostic reference harness
experiments.method: every pair on the public 2.1 leaderboard where one model runs under both, delta over the combined error bar
experiments.result: not constant and not the same sign. Gemini CLI is 8.1 points BELOW Terminus 2 on the same model; Codex is 5.1 above; two of five pairs are noise
experiments.note: RE-ANALYSIS of someone else's leaderboard, not an experiment I ran. It becomes mine the day I run Terminus 2 myself.

experiments.name: Does tailoring a document to its reader help?
experiments.hypothesis: a document rewritten for one specific reader beats the untouched original
experiments.method: 54 blind judges, three repeats per variant, one sentence changed at a time and everything else byte-identical
experiments.result: the tailored version scored lower and five times less stably, spread 0.83 against 0.17. Replicated three days apart on independent runs
experiments.note: run on my own instrument. Write-up is in a private repo.

experiments.name: Dip-buy rule, walk-forward
experiments.hypothesis: the dip-buy rule has an edge out of sample
experiments.result: no out-of-sample edge. Median held-out trade minus 50.3% of margin, n=9 and 5
experiments.note: underpowered and stated as such. It does not prove the rule is dead, only that there is no evidence it is alive. The strategy was shelved; the risk engine was kept.

projects.name: Ledger
projects.oneLiner: roadmaps, POCs, a send-performance harness, testing suites for clear signing, and the specifications for new features. a lot of architectural work on how things are supposed to work, for users and for the features themselves. mostly it is research distilled into what the hell can we do with this, how can it touch end users, and how can it move the needle. embedded apps, backend teams, nodes, infra.

projects.name: Anotherblock
projects.oneLiner: it was insanity. legal engineering of what even makes sense, and pitching almost free money to artists. they have so much unpublished material, progress that never sees the light. royalties are the more legal side; now they could sell their drafts, which was not mainstream or polished yet. we called all night pitching the new concept until we finally had a line-up, then worked on artwork and what else could be given. difficult to scale, though - like luxury you need scarcity and rarity, and an mp3 file just is not that.

projects.name: Etablera
projects.oneLiner: delivering projects end to end, managing expectations, negotiating, and learning that saying no helps. cheap clients and early annoyance lead to more of it later, not less. product marketing is the core of understanding what users want, and video editing and campaign launches are essential to knowing how things look and which angle to push. and organising hackathons and events is energetic.

projects.name: Wave Radio
projects.oneLiner: a way to channel my thoughts, and one of my favourite mediums. it lets me ask people hey, want to join my podcast. it ages well - a snapshot of what we were thinking. the ongoing obsession is whether it should be short format, and not wanting it to get too famous. it is almost an art project.

projects.name: RELAY → FAVOUR
projects.oneLiner: post a real-world favour and a World ID verified human goes and does it, with photo proof an AI checks. points first, and nothing of yours is ever held.

projects.name: Yieldbound
projects.oneLiner: agents do not need full wallets, they need bounded authority. lock the principal and let the agent spend only what the yield earns.

projects.name: RECEIPT
projects.oneLiner: signed, hash-linked receipts for agent work, then a TEE-attested score of whether the work was actually useful. an agent cannot pick its own grader.

projects.name: Gates

projects.name: NFT Safe Launch

projects.name: Mount Helicon
projects.oneLiner: the test-and-focus layer for ai agent memory: regression-tests what your agent retrieves, retires what is no longer true, turns memory state into cited next moves. ci for memory, with receipts.

projects.name: KYA
projects.oneLiner: signed safe/caution/block trust verdicts for any okx.ai agent, before you transact. the agent-vetting primitive the marketplace is missing.

projects.name: Overturn
projects.oneLiner: a prop-bet escrow that cannot pay out on a goal that did not happen.

projects.name: Litmus
projects.oneLiner: your crm is a firehose. sillage + fullenrich verify and de-noise it; litmus scores what's left against what you sell.

projects.name: Taste Machine

projects.oneLiner: an adversarial evaluation for the Kaggle AI Agent Security competition, multi-step tool attacks, 1,554 teams. submitted and scoring; not placed. repo still private.

projects.name: weirder-md
projects.oneLiner: six unusual ways to read a plain markdown file, and the live page rebuilds from git for someone who is not me.

projects.name: nullspace
projects.oneLiner: databases are built to store what is there. nullspace stores what was missing. every query that comes back empty gets filed, so you can see the shape of what people asked for and did not get. you ask the restaurant for a bottle of wine, they say no sir we do not have it, and nobody writes that down. this writes it down. built for datahub.

projects.name: pigeon
projects.oneLiner: API keys and env variables are a nightmare to hand around, and the models got sensitive about printing them in chat. the fix is a clipboard save, which I read on twitter and which nobody tells you. pigeon is the guided version for people new to vibe coding - one, two, three, and the key is in the native iCloud keychain for good.
